fuentes.titulo: Pausanias, Description of Greece 2. 29. 1 (trans. Jones) (Greek travelogue C2nd A.D.) :"[In the city of Epidauros in Argolis] is a precinct of Asklepios (Asclepius), with images of the god himself and Epione. Epione, they say, was the wife of Asklepios."

Suidas s.v. Epione (trans. Suda On Line) (Byzantine Greek lexicon C10th A.D.) :"Epione : wife of Asklepios (Asclepius), and daughters named Hygeia, Aigle (Aegle), Iaso, Akeso (Aceso), Panakeia (Panacea)."
